text:
Priya K: Heads-up — CI started failing nightly SAST runs with KMS decrypt errors after the RBAC tweak. saw: 

Priya K: [ci-job-123] error: KMS AccessDenied for projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/keystore/cryptoKeys/scanner-key: permissionDenied

Marco L: ugh, which RBAC tweak? we changed the scanner SA role last night right?

Priya K: yes, change was to remove roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter from project-editors and move to a narrower binding on service accounts. suspect scanner SA lost the binding.

Ben S: can you paste the service account email and the exact log? pinging @sec-bot for audit trail

Priya K: scanner-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com

sec-bot: Audit log: 2026-03-20T03:22:18Z grant.update by user:marco.l@redwood.com — removed principal:project-editors from role:roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter

Maya R: scanning job runs as scanner-sa via GKE workload identity. If the SA lost the key decrypt role the CI step will fail. Two remediation paths: rebind at key- or keyring-level with least privilege, or adopt short-lived decrypt via KMS signing service account token exchange.

Jordan P: for immediate unblock: re-add the role to scanner-sa on the specific key ring. Use: 
```bash
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding scanner-key \
  --location=global --keyring=keystore \
  --member=serviceAccount:scanner-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter
```

Ben S: also add an audit annotation: label the change with ticket ID so we can trace: SEC-2026-112

Priya K: doing that now, will run a dry-run in staging then apply to prod.

Maya R: after immediate fix we should discuss longer-term: 1) update premerge checklist so RBAC edits require sec review if they touch kms keys 2) create a gating SLO; CI should auto-fallback to a cached artifact for non-sensitive scans to avoid total job failure 3) add an automation that alerts if a key binding is removed from expected SAs

Marco L: agreed. Also found a flakey edge: when workload-identity mapping exists but SA lacks iam.serviceAccounts.get, the container still runs but can't impersonate properly. we should add that to the playbook.

Priya K: question: do we have a documented approver list for KMS key-level ACLs? I couldn't find it in the SOC docs.

Maya R: not formally. propose: add a KMS owners group: security-kms-approvers@redwood.com. Requirements: 2 approvers for prod key changes, 1 for staging. Add automation to require that group in the approval flow.

Jordan P: I'll open a PR to the runbook: /docs/runbooks/kms-rbac.md with the new approver flow + sample rollback snippet.

Ben S: for triage notes: add remediation steps and evidence to the SEC ticket: logs, gcloud policy before/after, and the patch that removed the binding (commit hash). That helps audits and reduces FP in future.

Priya K: applied the binding in prod, reran the nightly job. CI passed. leaving the thread open for postmortem notes and runbook PR link.

Maya R: can someone add a quick eval to Redwood Optimize to track scan-throughput after we change fallback caching? want to see perf/cost impact.

Marco L: noted. I'll coordinate with infra to instrument token latency and cache hit rates.

sec-bot: Ticket SEC-2026-112 created. Audit snapshot attached.

Priya K: thanks all :thumbsup: — will follow up with PR link and postmortem summary tomorrow.
